summary: Joseph plans to end his betrothal quietly, but an angel tells him Mary’s Child is from the Holy Spirit, so Joseph takes Mary home and names the Child Jesus.
key_insight: Matthew calls Joseph “a just man,” and the evidence he gives is mercy. Though he apparently believed Mary had been unfaithful, Joseph still refused to make her a public example. In him, righteousness and kindness were not rivals.
story: This is how the birth of Jesus Christ came about. Mary was betrothed to Joseph, but before they came together she was found to be with child “of the Holy Spirit.”
Joseph, her husband, was a just man. He did not want to make her a public example, so he decided to put her away secretly.

While he was thinking this over, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream: “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take to you Mary your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit. And she will bring forth a Son, and you shall call His name JESUS, for He will save His people from their sins.”
All this happened to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: “Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and bear a Son, and they shall call His name Immanuel,” which means “God with us.”

When Joseph woke up, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him and took Mary as his wife. But he had no union with her until she had given birth to her firstborn Son. And he called His name JESUS.

scene.label: Betrothal
scene.text: A betrothed couple were legally bound, so Matthew already calls Joseph “her husband” and Mary “your wife.” Ending a betrothal required a divorce. The law treated unfaithfulness during betrothal as adultery (Deuteronomy 22:23–24). Joseph could have brought a public charge; he chose the quietest path the law allowed.

scene.label: “Son of David”
scene.text: The angel addresses Joseph by his royal ancestry. By taking Mary home and naming the Child, Joseph received Jesus as his legal son. That is how Jesus, though not Joseph’s natural son, became heir to the royal line Matthew has just traced.

scene.label: The name
scene.text: Jesus is the Greek form of the Hebrew Yeshua, or Joshua, meaning the LORD saves. The angel explains it: “He will save His people from their sins.” The salvation promised goes deeper than rescue from Rome.

scene.label: Isaiah’s sign
scene.text: Isaiah gave the sign of Immanuel to King Ahaz around 735 BC, when Judah was threatened by Syria and Israel (Isaiah 7:1–14). Many hold that it had a first meaning in Ahaz’s day and its full meaning in Jesus; others see it as pointing directly to the Messiah. Matthew sees it fulfilled in a virgin’s Son who is truly God with us.

witnesses.matthew: Only Matthew tells the story from Joseph’s side. It explains how Jesus could be the Son of David through Joseph while being conceived by the Holy Spirit, and it gives the first of Matthew’s many fulfillment sayings: “that it might be fulfilled.” The name “God with us” at the start of his Gospel matches Jesus’ last words in it: “I am with you always” (Matthew 28:20).

seeing.reveals: Jesus is “God with us,” and He came to “save His people from their sins.” His names declare both who He is and what He came to do.
seeing.living: Joseph obeyed as soon as he woke, though it meant taking a wife others might whisper about and raising a Son who was not his by birth. When God’s word costs you your own plans and your good name, Joseph shows the way: get up and do what God said.
seeing.ponder: Is there something God has made plain to you that you are still thinking about instead of doing?

preaching.big_idea: The Child named Jesus is God with us, come to save His people from their sins.
preaching.watch_for: Notice the two names in verses 21 and 23. “JESUS” tells what He will do; “Immanuel” tells who He is. The Savior from sin is God Himself, present with His people.

title: An Angel Speaks to Joseph
